candidates.headline: PSX Closing Bell: Every Rose Has Its Thorn
candidates.summary: Tuesday confirmed close detail (same Strait-of-Hormuz selloff already logged above at impact 5; this is Mettis's own closing-bell print, published Jul 14, 2026 4:03pm PKT, with sector breakdown not previously captured): KSE-100 closed at 173,518.81, down 6,408.23 points (-3.56%); volume 409.23m shares, value traded Rs45.61bn, 620,763 trades across 498 companies; breadth 40 higher, 439 lower, 19 unchanged; top losers GHNI -8.74%, TRG -8.21%, GAL -8.01%, AKBL -7.65%, MLCF -7.55%; sole listed top gainer UPFL +0.36%. Reason given: 'escalating geopolitical tensions and a surge in global oil prices' after Trump's 20% Hormuz-transit fee and Iranian port blockade announcement, triggering 'widespread risk-off sentiment.'

candidates.headline: PSX loses 2,321 points on geopolitical fears
candidates.summary: Published Jul 18, 2026 07:32am PKT, corroborating the Friday confirmed close already logged this cycle (KSE-100 175,802.79, down 2,320.78 pts / -1.3%; volume 621m shares, -15.73% WoD; value Rs29.8bn, -13.65%; nine large-caps incl. Engro Holdings, United Bank and Lucky Cement together cut 1,105 points via profit-taking, quoting Topline Securities that 'the index remained under pressure' on Strait of Hormuz supply-disruption concerns). New economic data not previously logged: Pakistan's current account deficit was $649m in June 2026, but FY26 as a whole closed with only a $139m current-account deficit; technology exports hit a record $4.6bn for FY26, up 21% YoY; the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) rose to 106.44 in June, its highest level since September 2018; net FDI for FY26 was $1.64bn, down 34% YoY.

candidates.headline: SBP likely to keep interest rate unchanged at 11.5% at July 27 MPC meeting, survey shows
candidates.summary: Published Jul 21, 2026: a Topline Securities survey found 97% of market participants expect the State Bank of Pakistan's Monetary Policy Committee to hold the policy rate at 11.5% when it meets July 27, 2026 (only 3% expect a 100bps cut), citing heightened geopolitical uncertainty and the recent rebound in international oil prices despite contained inflation; the SBP last reviewed policy on June 15, 2026, also holding at 11.5%. About 49% of respondents expect the rate to remain at 11.5% by December 2026 while 46% foresee further easing; Topline Research itself expects the rate to fall below 11.5% by year-end. This is a market-expectation survey ahead of the decision, not the decision itself - logged as impact 3 (notable/guidance) pending the actual MPC outcome on July 27.

candidates.headline: PSX ends lower for third straight session - KSE-100 confirmed Thursday close down 2,690.48 points
candidates.summary: Confirmed close, from Wednesday's confirmed close of 174,429.92: KSE-100 'closed at 171,739.45, down 2,690.48 points, or 1.54%'; volume 525.12m shares, value traded Rs23.43bn. Express Tribune's article body states 91 stocks gained, 372 declined and 30 were unchanged; top gainers named Attock Refinery (ATRL) +1.73%, Air Link Communication (AIRLINK) +2.1%, Cnergyico Pk (CNERGY) +2.23%; top losers named United Bank (UBL) -2.73%, Fauji Fertiliser (FFC) -1.61%, Engro Holdings (ENGROH) -2.3%, plus Lucky Cement and Hubco cited elsewhere in wire coverage of the same session as among the day's biggest negative point-contributors (collectively with UBL, FFC and ENGROH subtracting about 1,101 points from the index per a companion WebSearch snippet on the same story, which separately cited a narrower '9 advancers vs 91 decliners' breadth figure for the KSE-100's own 100 constituents versus the 91/372/30 all-share breadth quoted in the full article - both breadth readings are reported here as found, unreconciled, pending a primary DPS check). Topline Securities quoted: 'bears remained firmly in control of the local bourse as intensifying geopolitical tensions continued to dampen investor sentiment.' Driver: Iran-backed Houthi militants' claimed attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea (see the Brent-crude item already logged this cycle) and WTI crude surging to approximately $90/bbl. Third consecutive losing session; logged at impact 4 for the magnitude of the move (-1.54%) continuing the Middle East oil-driven risk-off pattern already flagged this cycle.

candidates.headline: KSE-100 intraday: index down 1,060.98 points by mid-morning Friday, extending the Middle East oil-driven slide
candidates.summary: Per PSX's own market-summary page (psx.com.pk/market-summary/, page captured 2026-07-24 11:25:02 PKT, market status 'Open'): KSE-100 at 170,678.46, down 1,060.98 points (-0.62%) from Thursday's confirmed close of 171,739.45. No sector/stock-level closing-bell narrative or confirmed final print located in sources reviewed as of this checkpoint (11:00 PKT); direction is consistent with the ongoing Houthi/Red Sea oil-driven risk-off narrative already logged this cycle. Flagged as an intraday read pending the official Friday close.
